name: Subspace ASC Center
desc: Sealed within the Planar Sphere is a mysterious fissure of the IPC's Anomaly Supervision & Containment Center. Within this facility, reason outranks intuition, and rules outrank reason.

effects.2: Increases the wearer's SPD by 6%. When the wearer's SPD reaches 145 or higher, increases all allies' Break Effect by 18% after entering combat. This effect cannot stack.

pieces.name: ASC Dark Fissure
pieces.desc: Sealed within the Planar Sphere is a mysterious fissure of the IPC's Anomaly Supervision & Containment Center. Within this facility, reason outranks intuition, and rules outrank reason.
pieces.backstory:
"The greatest danger in the ASC Center is never the contained, but your own curiosity." When the facility's researchers receive their hefty copy of Top Secret: Employee Handbook, this quote on the title page is bound to be the very first thing they notice. A quick flip through the pages, and they'll soon understand exactly what it means—

Containment Object ASC-028, "Playmate Seeker"
Trait: The Playmate Seeker appears to be a harmless household service robot. It designates any sapient being within a twenty-meter radius as its "playmate." The chosen "playmate" must survive a barrage of firearms and successfully escape its pursuit. After this, they will swap roles every five minutes until one party finds and destroys the other.
Containment Procedure: Contain the Playmate Seeker in a room mirrored on all six sides. There, it will play with itself forever, yet never be able to touch the "playmate" in the mirror.

Containment Object ASC-032, "Stealth Cloak"
!! IMPORTANT REMINDER: DO NOT FORGET THIS OBJECT EXISTS !!
Trait: ASC-032 will tempt researchers into putting it on, and whoever does so will immediately vanish from sight. This is not optical invisibility under the laws of physics. Rather, it causes observers to overlook the wearer's very existence, subconsciously concocting countless reasons to justify their disappearance.
...

Of course, the mysteries of the ASC Center extend far beyond the anomalies it contains. Its very existence seems to be an enigma, with access tightly locked down by its shadowy director, Yabuli.
Rumor has it that the ASC Center is itself one massive containment object, connected to a fissure no one has ever set foot in. But the researchers stationed here usually have no desire to stare into the truth, thanks to far too many cautionary tales:
"This is the Anomaly Supervision & Containment Center. When you step through these doors, please leave all cognition of common sense behind."

pieces.name: ASC Negative Film
pieces.desc: ASC Center's Object Zero usually manifests as a projector, yet few know what truly lies beneath.
pieces.backstory:
The ASC Center houses a vast and complex array of anomalies, yet "Object Zero" remains a mystery few can unravel.
Its archive records the information Yabuli went to great lengths to obtain—

Containment Object ASC-0, usually manifests as a film projector. Containment Class: Extreme.
It boasts unprecedented stability. Under the protection of a special substance, it rarely reacts chemically with other matter, which also means it cannot be dismantled.
Therefore, researchers highly suspect it only interacts with certain predetermined targets.
During a random moment of chaos, Object Zero briefly resonated with another contained object, the remnants of a compass excavated from a certain ruin.

"I heard it... the echoes of surging waves, the hiss of a flickering screen, a faint sigh..."
That was all the shaken researcher could report. After a few brief words, Object Zero once again returned to quiescence.
No one knows why Yabuli, or even the IPC, takes such a keen interest in Object Zero.

An anonymous conspiracy theorist once claimed on a deep web forum that it was all just a lie cooked up by Yabuli to lock down IPC resources. Others say the IPC has long been dissatisfied with stagnant profits, and that Object Zero holds the secret to a massive market. Once they get their hands on it, the destiny of this cosmos will change along with it...
